dek: Seven Rocky Mountain waterfalls with walk lengths, fees and the 2026 timed-entry rules. Copeland Falls is the shortest walk; Adams Falls is on the west side.
overview: Rocky Mountain National Park covers a bit over 415 square miles of northern Colorado, from montane meadows up to alpine tundra.

We cover seven waterfalls here. Adams Falls is on the west side near Grand Lake and has the most visitor reviews. The other six are filed under Estes Park on the east side. Walks range from Copeland Falls at 0.6 mile round trip to Cascade Falls at 3.5 miles one way (7 miles round trip). Bridal Veil Falls and Chasm Falls have no published distance.
fallsIntro: Alberta Falls is the Bear Lake Road hike, starting at Glacier Gorge Junction. Adams Falls is the west-side walk. In 2026 the two areas have different timed-entry rules, covered below.
plan: The two shortest walks are Copeland Falls (0.6 mile round trip, 15 feet of climbing, rated easy by the park) in the Wild Basin area and Adams Falls (about three-quarters of a mile round trip, about 150 feet of climbing) on the west side. They are at different entrances. Alberta Falls is 0.8 mile one way with 160 feet of climbing from Glacier Gorge Junction.
Ouzel Falls is the longer Wild Basin hike at 2.7 miles one way (5.4 round trip) with 950 feet of climbing. Cascade Falls on the North Inlet Trail is 3.5 miles one way (7 round trip) with 300 feet.
flow: The nearest gauge is the Loch Outlet in Loch Vale (USGS 401733105392404), about a mile from Alberta Falls. From 2019 through 2024 its average daily flow peaked in June at about 25 cubic feet per second and was zero in January.
Those numbers describe one small stream, so use them as a rough guide to when water runs highest, not a flow report for each waterfall.
feesLead: Budget for the entrance pass and, on the dates below, a $2 reservation fee. They are separate charges.
access: From May 22 through October 12, 2026, a timed-entry reservation is required to enter between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m. Bear Lake Road needs its own reservation from 5 a.m. to 6 p.m., May 22 through October 18. You book on Recreation.gov, and it is in addition to the entrance pass. Entering before 9 a.m. or after 2 p.m. doesn't need the park-wide reservation. Passes are sold at entrance stations, which take cards only.
safety: The park rates Copeland Falls easy, and Adams Falls is a short walk with about 150 feet of climbing. The longer trails climb several hundred feet. We have no waterfall-specific warnings on file, so check trail conditions with the park before you head out.
